title: MusicManager.cs
summary: Self-bootstrapping persistent singleton that plays background music. Each scene plays the track set in Resources/SceneMusicMap, crossfading from the previous one; Options > Audio can skip to the next playlist track or stop the music. It also fades out for menus, ducks while settings are open, and keeps its volume synced to the 'Mindscape.Music' PlayerPrefs setting. Never placed in a scene manually.

notes.match: public static MusicManager Instance { get; private set; }
notes.text: Singleton reached by the static helpers below (Next, Stop, Play, PlayTrack, FadeOut...), so any script can call MusicManager.PlayTrack(...) without a reference.
Same PlayerPrefs key the Options and Pause music sliders write to.
Stop / Play in Options > Audio is remembered here, so the music stays off across scenes and sessions.
Raised when the track changes or the music is stopped or started; the Options > Audio "now playing" line listens to it.

notes.match: AudioSource _source;    // the track the player hears
notes.text: Two AudioSources are used so one track can fade out while the next fades in (the crossfade).
The Resources/SceneMusicMap asset: which track each scene (by name prefix) plays, tracks kept out of the playlist, and the crossfade length.

notes.match: readonly List<AudioClip> _tracks = new List<AudioClip>(); // the Next-track playlist (_all minus reserved tracks)
notes.text: Everything in Resources/Music is loaded; reserved tracks (named in the map) only play where an entry names them and are left out of the Next playlist.
Runs automatically before the first scene loads, so music exists from the very first frame without anyone placing it in a scene.
Survives scene loads, so the music does not restart on every level.
The intro holds the music while its story video plays, then resumes it for the title card.
Skips to the next playlist track with a short crossfade. A scene's own track may be outside the playlist (index -1), in which case Next starts the playlist.
Plays a Resources/Music track by name now; a scene can call it mid-story (the Chapter 3 Episode 8 walk does).

notes.match: public static void FadeTo(float level, float seconds = 0.5f)
notes.text: Sets a target level (0 to 1 of the volume setting) that Update eases toward. FadeOut is FadeTo(0).
Lowers the music to about 40% while settings are open so the volume sliders can be heard, then restores it.

notes.match: public static void LoadSceneFaded(string sceneName, float seconds = 0.8f)
notes.text: Fades the music out, then loads the scene, so leaving to the menu has no hard cut.
Falls back to the built-in defaults if the map asset is missing.
Sorted by name so the Next order is stable.

notes.match: Debug.LogWarning("MusicManager: no music found in Resources/Music.");
notes.text: Warns and does nothing if the folder is empty.
Adds the two AudioSources at runtime (no prefab needed), looping and silent until a track is switched in.
The scene's mapped track, else whatever is already playing, else the first playlist track. A mapped name with no clip logs a warning.

This is the only background music. A scene with its own looping music source would play a second track on top, so any other long looping source is silenced as the scene loads. Short loops (alarms, engines) stay.
Crossfades to the clip: the old source becomes the outgoing one and fades away while the new one fades in. It plays unless the music is stopped or held by the intro; the same clip carries on.
Only reads PlayerPrefs ten times a second instead of every frame.
Final volume = the Settings slider x any fade-out level x the settings duck, then each source's own crossfade weight.
